item.text: I’m going to trace the failing parser branch first, keep the surface area tight, and only touch the minimum code needed to make the test pass. After that I’ll run the relevant checks so we can verify the fix without drifting into unrelated cleanup.

The shell wrapper is hitting the sandbox boundary before the command can even start, so I’m trying a simpler probe to confirm whether this is a general local-command limitation or just the first command shape. Once I know that, I can choose the least invasive path to inspect the parser branch.

I’m blocked from reading the workspace because every local shell command is failing before execution with `sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`.

To keep the patch constrained to the one parser branch, I need one of these from you:
1. The failing test output, plus the parser file/branch it points to.
2. The relevant parser file and the test file contents pasted here.
3. Permission to proceed using a different repo-access path if one is available in your environment.

Once I have that, I’ll make the smallest possible fix and verify just the affected test path.
